answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. The practical upshot is that honesty is the only strategy that scales — a farm that tries to game the system pays for each identity it adds. Consider a sparrow as the anchor of the cost.
